items.text: Content
Added the researcher’s final chip.
New chips now count toward the achievement.
Fuel cell recipes have been removed from the crafting machine.
Gameplay
Passing out after 2:00 is now enforced more reliably.
Players can no longer clip through walls from knockback caused by the Coptch or any other enemy.
Fixes to fishing animations.
Farm
Crops should no longer grow inconsistently.
Improved accuracy when planting trees; they should no longer disappear.
Other
A ladder down should now appear after breaking all the rocks in the mines.
Ark trophies should be visible again.
UI
Various improvements to the quest panel UI and processing machines.
The cursor should no longer appear after making a donation with a controller.
I am always so excited to share new updates with you.

We are getting close to 4 years of working on Farlands, and being able to keep adding new content and improving the experience is great. This time, we are also bringing you the biggest update Farlands will ever receive.

Version 1.2 comes with more than 70 new items, machines that change how some familiar items are obtained, changes to rewards and progression, and a complete rework of the upgrade costs for tools and the ship. There is a lot to explain, so let us go through it step by step.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/a79faecc688b98cbd1b609ed0226acaea8368b77.gif"]
We have introduced 11 machines in Farlands that process resources and turn them into other resources:
Furnaces will allow you to obtain ingots, a new material introduced in this update.
The Biocompressor, Energitron and Trienergitron will allow you to obtain fuel cells.
The Polymerizer is used to obtain plastic and silicone, two new items that will be used to upgrade the ship.
The Preserver will allow you to turn your fruit and vegetables into juices, jams and pickles, increasing their value.
The Seeder will allow you to turn harvested vegetables into seeds, so you will not have to buy more if you do not want to.
The Recycler will return the materials from furniture you have crafted but no longer want.
The Researcher is the new way to obtain furniture set chips. It will sequentially request resources from every planet, and delivering them will unlock the corresponding sets.

Finally, the Dimensional Exchanger is a strange portal to another dimension that will give you random items in exchange for large amounts of resources. It can even unlock the new Golden Furniture Set, which can only be obtained through this strange machine.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/9c40b3abd8d2e765d04b304d6ebeb38ecd79a393.gif"]
These machines introduce new items that will be used for upgrades to both tools and the ship: ingots, silicone and plastic.
This change addresses feedback from some players who felt that upgrades were too simple, that the experience felt a little too vanilla, and that everything could be obtained using money alone.

Money will still remain an option because it has always been a design decision that you should be able to complete Farlands in whichever way you enjoy most, without being forced to engage with systems you do not enjoy. However, doing so now requires a little more exploration across the planets and some mineral processing, adding an extra layer of management that this playstyle did not originally have.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/512cac92ac1b43a3d2e1d5fb9e02e181203a0db4.gif"]

Many of these machines change the way you interact with progression in the game. Some elements will be harder to obtain while others will be easier. As a result, the way these machines and their crafting chips are obtained is spread throughout the entire game.

Some are obtained by exploring the mines, while others are rewards from the Ark. We will continue making adjustments so that progression feels as smooth as possible, but everything is already set up to unlock naturally throughout a normal playthrough.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/818ae55f8d7b851fcede8787feb6fd75451707db.gif"]

notes.title: WHAT IF I HAVE ALREADY COMPLETED THE GAME?

items.text: If you have progressed far enough in your save to have missed some of these rewards, you will receive an email containing the machines you should have obtained. This way, we make sure nobody is left without essential items required to keep playing properly.
Even so, given how extensive the changes in this update are, we believe this is a very good time to start a new save and experience how the entire progression of Farlands changes with this update.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/3fb22b21dd4f09c2aeb84dcc4968928789f799de.gif"]

As a small bonus in this update, we have added buttons to sort chests and send all duplicate items to the chest. It is a small feature, but it slightly improves the user experience, something we are always trying to refine.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/4f31599bfc89e4ac8f25fd8defdef872d229596d.gif"]

For more advanced players, especially those with chests full of resources and no idea what to do with them, the Dimensional Exchanger will become your friend. You will be able to throw in all those resources and receive useful rewards and items intended for the very end of the game.

If you have hundreds of spare stones, stored minerals or chests full of items, absolutely everything can be thrown into the Dimensional Exchanger. Using a tier system, you can overload it so that the following day it gives you a random item.

This can include cooked dishes, machines or the new Golden Furniture Set, a small tribute to the classic Harvest Moon games and a way to make use of all those resources. This set does not have a crafting chip and can only be obtained through the Dimensional Exchanger.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/347f2715b14a99acb94f47f10cf4bd66d07a0ef5.png"]

Over the next few weeks we will continue balancing all of these changes, while also working on update 1.3, which should arrive relatively soon and improve one of the systems that currently needs a little extra attention. We will talk more about that when the time comes.
For now, thank you very much for your continued support. I hope this update encourages you to return to your existing saves or start new ones.
Best wishes!

releases.displayName: Farlands Soundtrack update, and more is on the way

items.text: Hello everyone!

Even though Farlands 1.0 is already out, we want you to know that we're still working hard to improve the experience as much as possible. In fact, we're even working on more content for the game, but you'll start seeing more about that over the next few weeks. I don't want to spoil the surprise just yet.
For now, I just wanted to let you know that the soundtrack has been updated to include the final versions of every track.

Carlos and Enoc, Farlands' composers, have been working hard to create a strong and cohesive musical identity for the entire game. These new versions reflect all of their effort and dedication, replacing the earlier versions and adding a few tracks that were still missing.

With that said, we're keeping a very close eye on your feedback so we can continue improving Farlands with every update. There'll be a patch later this week with a ton of fixes and optimizations, and we'll soon have more news to share about what's coming next.
And just a heads-up: it's going to be big.
Weddings should now work correctly in both Terbin and Galea.
Spike's and Eddy's event 5 should now trigger correctly.
Tables reactivate correctly after Siona's event.
Alisha now sends the correct email after completing her event.
Siona's email with the cake now actually includes the cake.
Adjustments to some dialogues and updated Siona's avatar.
Sprinklers: fixed watering so it works correctly, fixed the issue with multiple sprinklers and seeds being deleted after placing them.
Loading of crop robeets is now more stable.
Fixed the removal of tilled soil containing a seed, and the energy consumption when watering an already-watered tile.
Optimized resource consumption when picking up an item, especially when the inventory is full.
Added a check for inventory stacks at 0.
Added a check on items so they can't be placed in unavailable areas.
The crafting machine now accounts for multiple stacks.
The crystal bee drops to the ground if the inventory is full.
Mine stairs should now work as intended.
Enemies are forcibly removed when defeated, and their SFX stops correctly.
Adjusted the sale value of balloons so they don't break the economy.
Fixed the size of the large blue rug and the height of the pyramid.
Fixed the Droid's description in the social window.
Updated the IDs of fences and floors.
Greater robustness when loading ark donations.
Reinforced the logic for talking to Bob; we now can't talk to him while he's hiding in the arena.
Achievements
-The "harvest all vegetables" achievement should now be awarded correctly.
Crafting
-Added the Icomelon recipe.
-Items can no longer be crafted with a full inventory, preventing item loss.
Matter Processor
-The matter processor can no longer be closed until the progress bar has stopped.
Dialogues
-Various fixes.
-Fixed freezes when talking to some characters.
Fishing
-Taking damage while fishing now interrupts the action.
Speeder
-Various fixes
NPCs
-Fixed Elliot's sprite at the farm.
-Adjusted Zoe's path so it no longer overlaps with Gorg.
-Layla now gives 1 typewriter instead of 10.
-Adjusted the position of some NPCs so they no longer block entrances.
-Fixed descriptions for some NPCs in the character panel.
Economy
-The end-of-day window should now display earnings correctly.
UI
-The travel panel should now display correctly on ultra-wide monitors.
-Close buttons have been implemented in all windows.
-Improved controller navigation in the relationships window.
-The ark's donation menu should no longer have duplicate green borders.
Audio
-Added sound effects for Bob.
Other
-Rebalanced relationship points when interacting with romanceable NPCs; it now costs less to improve relationships.
-Added lighting inside the ship.
Removed the spawn for an insect that was cut during Early Access (the Vanadian wasp).
Adjusted several areas and layers in Vanadian so rocks and other details display correctly.
Restored the pyramid layers in Vanadian.
Fixed collisions near the water and in the oxygen area in Darmstad.
Adjusted the map boundary in the Darmstad mine.
Fixed duplicated Chinese dialogue and various typos.
Added missing Chinese and Japanese characters to the fonts.
Improved the behaviour of the options menu when configuring controls.
Fixed and standardised the exit button across several interfaces.
Added progress information and icons to load slots.
Adjusted the size of the progress indicator when loading a game.
Reactivated the lighting in the resources section.
Fixed fishing-related issues.
Adjusted the ship panel during the speeder event.
Fixed the player’s starting position in the speeder event.
Improved the speeder’s overall behaviour.
Updated the button prompt shown in the speeder tutorial.
Adjusted animations in several speeder events.
Fixed the day on which the first summer email is received.
Fixed item counting when picking up multiple units of the same item.
Iriel and Te’Kragh no longer remain in fixed positions.
The player can no longer move during the dialogue that follows a donation.
Moved an Ark event trigger to prevent it from overlapping with a delivery.
The Nori and Amadeus event no longer triggers unless there are at least two free inventory slots.
The late-arrival message no longer breaks when changing the resolution.
Adjusted cameras and reference points in several events.
Fixed the position of two incorrectly placed event objects.
Fixed a reference related to the electric guitar.

The 0.9 Update focuses on just two things: Weddings and the Ark rework. And while this update may seem smaller on paper, both features are extremely important and come with a lot of additions to Farlands. Let’s go step by step.
With this update, you can now complete the stories of all romanceable characters by reaching their final relationship event, the Level 5 event.

The eight bachelor and bachelorette storylines now reach their conclusion, closing their character arcs. But that doesn’t mean the journey ends there, because once you reach this level with any NPC, and if you have enough space in your house, you’ll be able to get married.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/9da6267a1c2d912d06fe8bd6d3021cec19e1d3fd.gif"]
To get married, you’ll need to use the Ceremonial Ribbon. Mayor Oola will explain how everything works when the time comes.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/400de376417eabf9ba4d3ea9e4a6d61a245288f7.gif"]
After the wedding, your husband or wife will move into your house and will accompany you on some of your trips.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/1443859db9e7a5200d58381ea4d087b37e413fde.gif"]
All of this adds up to 25 new events and hundreds of new lines of dialogue, bringing the entire relationship system in Farlands to its conclusion.

Alongside this, we’ve also been working on improving the gamefeel and overall functionality of the Ark. Since this system was introduced very early in Farlands’ development, time had started to show its effects, and it was due for a full overhaul.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/4b8e81ac606cc935fd8bb7c88dc477ba5b1219ce.gif"]

This includes redesigned interfaces that better communicate the Ark’s progress, new animations that show the museum filling up over time, and improved visual and audio feedback for every step of the process.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/f1a6329ddc505284384672ccaa6f55fd42bb0d39.gif"]
As always, we’ve also fixed a large number of smaller bugs, with the goal of making Farlands feel as smooth as possible. And at this point… we’re getting close to the end.
The next update will bring Farlands to version 1.0, with all the content planned in the roadmap in place, and even a few extras that weren’t originally announced, like the speeder, just to name one.

It’s incredible to see how close we are to finishing the project. Even though we plan to keep updating the game after 1.0 with fixes and small additions, we are truly approaching the end of the road, and none of this would have been possible without you.
So thank you very much.
Now the team goes back into the cave to keep working on Farlands, and the next time we update you, it will be to share information about the final release date.
This update was supposed to arrive soon, but I will not lie to you: We got carried away adding things and may have gone a bit overboard.

Version 0.7 was meant to be the “quality of life update”, so we spent these past months reviewing all the feedback you have been leaving on Discord and smoothing out all those small rough edges that create friction during gameplay.
The list of changes and additions is huge, so I will not go through everything, but here are some of the most important highlights.
You can now move items in chests using fewer buttons, making them much more comfortable to use.
The toolbar now disappears when you walk close to it, so it will no longer block your view.
The crafting UI has received a full rework and is now clearer and easier to use.
You can now remap buttons however you like.
A new tutorial system has been implemented. It is faster, simpler, and clearer.
The fishing system has been fully reworked. There are no more weird animations or awkward controller grips.
You can now interact with objects directly from the toolbar and see tooltips on shop items.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/f259aff8245dbbfcb65c803a390852414a29ee83.gif"]
Robeets are now shown on the toolbar, and you will be notified when you have enough for an upgrade.
Vegetable growth times have been shortened to make all of Farlands faster and more dynamic.
You will now find credits by performing regular in game actions.
Gamefeel has been improved across several interfaces, such as the end of day screen, the matter processor, and everything that happens inside the Ark.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/3fc8e3ac5602298d93b280cedd2118c94911eaa5.gif"]
And so many bugs have been fixed that if we listed them all, we would be here all day.
But that is not all. An update that only fixes and improves existing systems is not especially exciting for players (even if it is great for us), so this update also includes:
Ten new events. Eight are for romanceable candidates and two are story events. And most importantly of all, this update brings the speeder.

After progressing far enough in the story, Te’Kragh will give you your very own speeder, allowing you to travel across the planets of SR755 at maximum speed. It does not consume anything and will always be with you, just one button away, so make sure to use it.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/e7d90f6df92e73a5b64dcadec36a206e92082f95.gif"]

That said, there are still a few things from 0.7 that we have put aside to avoid delaying the update any further. Over the next few weeks, you can expect some additional tweaks related to onboarding and various events.

After that, version 0.8 is already taking shape and will include one of the last major systems still missing from Farlands, livestock farming. So do not go too far, because 2026 will be the year of Farlands.
This update brings two big new features, plus a bunch of smaller ones that make everything feel more polished. Let’s start with the big ones.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/7c53cf0db8dc5e4b03b6d73902445ba9417cc096.gif"]
Vanadian, the labyrinth-like desert of SR755, comes to Farlands with new resources, a unique day-night cycle, and a merchant packed with fresh and interesting stuff.

When you land, look for Bob the merchant. He sells unique seeds, new furniture, and strange artifacts. But since he’s a desert dweller, you’ll need to track him down across different areas of the planet.
Be careful if you arrive at night, because instead of insects, hostile mobs you’ll normally see in the mines will spawn.
And do you see that buried pyramid? It might be hiding something important for late game...
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/265d6e4a0c8ed3b19867996ee08d2c59a1a08eb7.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/af040aebebbaa25769a75e236e43a0b557a3b924.gif"]

Nine new events have been added to Farlands, seven on Terbin and two on Galea. Unlike the story events, these ones appear if you travel to those planets on specific days. They’re small events, but they’re a great chance to see new NPC interactions, buy unique items and artifacts from shops, and dive a little deeper into the world of Farlands and its characters.
With this new event type, you’ll now see icons on the system map showing available events. That includes story, tutorials, bachelors, and this new calendar events.
After those two big new additions, let’s go through the smaller ones:
New story event: You can now see up to 50% of the story.
Options improvements: Windowed mode and resolutions.
New furniture sets: Vanadian inspired.
New collectible: The Floots, scattered all across the system. They’re not required for 100% but they’re pretty cool.
New recipe chip shop: Iriel now sells chips and food.
New lighting system in Terbin, Bohr, and Galea: Each planet gets dark at different hours, so watch out.
New animations for Iriel and Te’Kragh
General bug fixing

Now it’s time to work on 0.7, the quality of life update. Truth is, we already have it pretty far along, but all that progress will “get spent” because first we need to update the Unity version we’re using, and that might break some things.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43546864/e7d90f6df92e73a5b64dcadec36a206e92082f95.gif"]

We need to do this because Farlands started on a Unity version that will soon lose support. It’s better to rip off the band-aid now and make the jump to a newer version right alongside the quality of life update.
We’ve already tested it and it doesn’t seem too bad, but even so Rubén and Néstor, our programmers, will spend a couple of weeks making sure nothing explodes and all systems hold up fine.
Once we get past that hurdle, we’ll let you know and continue with the roadmap toward 0.7, which should arrive sometime in October (fingers crossed).
Thanks so much for your support and enjoy 0.6!

Hello everyone! It's been a few weeks since the last update and it's about time we bring you all up to date, so let's get straight to the point:
In two weeks update 0.4 will arrive!
This update focuses mainly on NPCs, bachelors, dialogs and mails.
To give you an idea of the scope of this update, we estimate that over 1000 new lines of dialogue will be added to Farlands!

That is: The first love event with each bachelor and bachelorette, emails that you will be able to receive on your PDA, dialogues that will vary depending on the progress of the story or your relationship with the NPCs... The complete pack.
We are convinced that this update will be very worthwhile and will give a new (and expected) layer of depth to Farlands to bring the game a little closer to version 1.0.
We will update you very shortly with all the details of what this new update will include, so stay tuned.

Let's not pretend, in the last few weeks the whole Farlands team has been a bit hidden and not saying much. But it was for a reason: Update 0.3 is already available, and the amount of content it adds to the game is dizzying.
With this out the way, let's get started!
ACHIEVEMENTS

One of the most requested things by the community; a very large list of achievements with objectives to accomplish, has been added to Farlands. In total there are 50 achievements, although since many of them cannot be obtained yet. Only those that can be obtained will be available on Steam, the rest will be added in later updates.
The achievement system is also integrated into the game, in one of the collections tabs, and connected to Steam, granting players the achievements retroactively.
TOOL UPGRADE SYSTEM
A classic of the management games, but that has taken us some time because of the complexity of the system.
From now on, talking to Gorg in Terbin, you will be able to upgrade your primary tools, by doing so, in addition to increasing their power, the tools will expand their range of action.
Using them in the mine is very rewarding.
FOOD

And just talking about the mine. A system that is more than necessary to be able to advance more easily and make the most of the days, is the food system, which from this update is now fully functional.

In the crafting machine, gathering the necessary ingredients, you will be able to cook different dishes to recover energy. My personal recommendation: Farmer's tea, although you have about 30 different dishes available to try out recipes.
HOUSE UPGRADE SYSTEM

And this is still going on, your house can now be upgraded by talking to Grubert, the carpenter of Galea. For a small fee and some resources, he will use his carpentry skills to fix and enlarge your house.
NEW FURNITURE AND INTERIOR DECORATION

And what to do with a huge mansion? Decorate it, of course. Because from 0.3 you will be able to craft more than 40 new pieces of furniture, and use them both indoors and outdoors. The sprites that have accompanied you at home since day 1, you can now remove them, they are now furniture with which you can interact.
GUESTS AND BETTER NPC

And if you visit Terbin to buy some of the chips needed to unlock the furniture crafts, you may find spaceships parked next to yours. These ships are from guests who have come to visit the system to have a drink, at the moment there are only a few, but they will be expanded with easter eggs, references and funny dialogues, a way to give life and personality to the settlement of Terbin.
And Terbin has even more things: Until now they were still sprites, but from 0.3 they will move around the town in random routes, bringing a lot of life to the town.
MORE STORY AND NEW CHARACTERS

Finally, a new story fragment is available in Galea, where you can also meet three new characters and their adorable companions, who were hiding behind the workers' fences, although that's best to find out for yourselves.
IMPORTANT

This update brings multiple new systems, so we expect at least a couple of weeks of bugs and inconsistencies that we will be fixing in small patches, even if Farlands is being completed slowly, it is still an Early Access. Nothing particularly serious should happen, but keep in mind, as always, that we will gradually patch anything that is buggy.
Also, one of the systems that was supposed to be added in this update: Weather, is not yet finished, so we have decided to delay it a bit, so it will arrive in a patch a bit later.
That being said, thank you very much for your time and enjoy the new update while we work on the next one!
It's been two months since the Early Access launch of Farlands and the whole team is thrilled with the reception it's had, so we'd like to thank you for your support right from the start!
But even though the launch went very well, we haven't stopped working since release, and to date we've released no less than 17 patches with fixes for dozens and dozens of bugs!
Starting with the Ark, map and neighbors tabs in the main menu:

In the neighbors tab you will be able to see a provisional list of all Farlands NPCs, in update 0.4, (the update that will include the social elements), this tab will be updated, but for now it will be enabled as a list of all the characters in the game.
In the map tab you will be able to see the entire SR755 system, its planets, where you are located and how many fuel cells the ship has left, to know its location even if you are far away from it.

And finally, in the Ark tab you will be able to see all the collections of items you have donated, to keep track of your progress. And later on, you will be able to see your achievements, although you will have to wait a bit longer for that.
Along with these tabs, the main menu starts to show some information about each game, to make it easier to differentiate them and see where they are in the game.
The crafting machine is now upgraded!
Scattered around the stores, you can now find upgrade chips for your crafting machine. If you buy them and place them in the machine, you will unlock new crafting recipes.
And obviously, with this new system, a new set of outdoor furniture is added, the mushroom furniture set, which is crafted using mainly Bohr's moon mushrooms.
Finally, a new fragment of the main story has been added to the adventure, you will be able to unlock it by playing normally, whether you make a new game, or continue with yours.
Steam cards, badges and stuff!

Along with these changes, although outside the game itself, from now on you will get Steam trading cards while playing Farlands. With those cards you will be able to earn badges and unlock backgrounds and icons to customize your Steam page.
The update 0.2, is the update that brings less content of all the Farlands roadmap, this was done on purpose to make room for those first weeks of fighting against bugs and important fixes.
However, I hope you can enjoy these small additions and stay tuned for the next update, 0.3, which will bring mountains of content that will extend the life of Farlands a lot.
